record.action: Add an interlock on HV-QW-B-IN and HV-QW-B-OUT that prevents opening unless HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT are both confirmed open.
record.reason: The scenario occurs when quench water valves open early per proc:P-REB-START-2 while shell-side block valves remain closed, isolating the relief path. An engineered interlock directly prevents the out-of-sequence operation that defeats RV-PATH-EA425B, preferred over procedure revision alone.

record.action: Install a hydrocarbon detector on quench-water inlet line L-QW-B-IN with an automatic trip that closes HV-QW-B-IN and HV-QW-B-OUT and raises an alarm on detection of hydrocarbons.
record.reason: The PRV RV-PATH-EA425B does not protect against composition change in the quench loop; detecting hydrocarbons and isolating the quench loop prevents accumulation of flammable mixture after a tube rupture.

record.action: Install a check valve in line L-A-SOUT to prevent reverse flow from DA-406 into EA-425A when SV-421QA/QB fail to open.
record.reason: The gap arises because DA-406 overpressure pushes liquid/vapor back through L-A-SOUT into EA-425A when its relief valves fail. A check valve in L-A-SOUT directly blocks the backflow path, addressing the consequence independent of the fire cause or relief valve reliability.

record.action: Add a valve-position interlock (limit switches) that prevents opening quench-water valves HV-QW-B-IN and HV-QW-B-OUT unless process-side valves HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT are confirmed open, and include this interlock in P-REB-START-2.
record.reason: The relief valve RV-PATH-EA425B is not credited because inlet valve HV-B-SIN is closed; the interlock eliminates the operator error that leaves process valves closed while heat is applied.

record.action: Install a check valve on line L‑B‑SIN (DA‑406 to EA‑425B) to block reverse flow into the standby reboiler shell.
record.reason: Closed HV‑B‑SIN/SOUT block the relief path; a check valve directly stops the reverse flow that overfills EA‑425B.

record.action: Fit a valve-position interlock (limit switches) on HV-QW-A-OUT and HV-QW-A-IN so that HV-QW-A-IN cannot be opened unless HV-QW-A-OUT is verified open, and add a check in P-REB-START-2 confirming HV-QW-A-OUT open.
record.reason: The relief valve RV-PATH-EA425A is only credited if HV-A-SIN is managed; the root cause is closing HV-QW-A-OUT while heat continues, so preventing that closure removes the overpressure driver.

record.action: Install an independent high-pressure trip on column DA-406 (new pressure transmitter PT-DA-406) that automatically closes quench-water inlet valves HV-QW-A-IN and HV-QW-B-IN when column pressure exceeds a set point below the relief valve set pressure.
record.reason: The scenario’s cause is premature opening of relief valves SV-421QA/QB; an independent trip stops heat input before the relief valves can open, addressing the hazard directly.

record.action: Install a key-lock open (car-seal) on manual block valve HV-A-SIN and add a verification step in procedure P-REB-START-1 to confirm HV-A-SIN is open before reboiler startup.
record.reason: The credited relief valve RV-PATH-EA425A only works if inlet valve HV-A-SIN is open; it is currently unmanaged, so securing HV-A-SIN open removes the cause of low flow and enables the relief valve.

record.action: Lock open HV-A-SIN (or add it to the managed valve program with position monitoring) to match HV-A-SOUT which is already locked open.
record.reason: RV-PATH-EA425A is credited but only at pfd_if_isolatable because HV-A-SIN is unmanaged. Locking it open or managing its position ensures the relief path remains available during external fire, closing the gap without adding new equipment.

record.action: Install a tube‑rupture detection system (differential pressure transmitter) on heat exchanger EA‑425B with automatic closure of its process‑side and quench‑water isolation valves.
record.reason: The existing relief valve RV‑PATH‑EA425B only addresses overpressure, not tube rupture; detection and isolation directly prevents cross‑contamination.

record.action: Install a dedicated thermal relief valve on EA-425B shell side independent of HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT, or add HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT to the managed valve program locked open when EA-425B is in service.
record.reason: RV-PATH-EA425B is not credited because its inlet valves HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT are closed, leaving the exchanger with no relief path during external fire. A local relief valve or managed open block valves removes the isolation that defeats the existing relief path.

record.action: Erect vehicle‑impact barriers (bollards/guardrails) around line S‑L‑A‑SIN in LOC‑OLEFINS‑UNIT.
record.reason: No layer addresses vehicle impact; a physical barrier removes the cause of line rupture.

record.action: Provide a dedicated, pilot‑operated relief valve on reboiler EA‑425A (RV‑PATH‑EA425A) with independent actuation and ensure its inlet valves are locked open for fire scenarios.
record.reason: No protection layer exists for external fire; an independent engineered relief valve gives reliable overpressure protection.

record.action: Revise procedure P-REB-START-2 to add a mandatory hold point with independent verification that HV-B-SIN and HV-B-SOUT are open before opening HV-QW-B-IN/HV-QW-B-OUT, and install a local shell-side pressure alarm that activates if quench water flow starts while block valves are closed.
record.reason: This target has zero protection layers against the procedural error of opening quench water early. The procedure revision adds a procedural barrier with verification, and the pressure alarm provides an engineered detection layer that alerts operators to the hazardous condition before overpressure.
